findings.title: Stop hook lets a turn end red on 2 of 65 policy-corpus files (AGENTS.md, dev/audit/README.md)
findings.claim: With the policy linter red and the turn's only change one policy-corpus file, the production Stop hook exits 0 (turn ends unrefused) for 2 of the 65 files policy_lint --corpus-filter prints: AGENTS.md and dev/audit/README.md.
findings.mechanism: stop-selfcheck.sh decides whether to run policy_lint by a hand-kept prefix list (POLICY_PREFIXES). It covers the old home of the audit README (tools/audit/) but not its new one (dev/audit/README.md, moved in the reorganisation), and it never listed AGENTS.md, which CLAUDE.md names as binding and policy_lint measures. The hook's own comment says a prefix list that is too narrow is 'the failure that matters'; its self-test pins only the paths it lists.

evidence.unit: corpus files the hook lets through red
evidence.contention_note: box shared with other seats' runs; a count, contention-immune

findings.instrumented_symbol: .claude/hooks/stop-selfcheck.sh:POLICY_PREFIXES (touches_policy), driven end to end through the hook's main path in a scratch repo

perturbation.change: POLICY_PREFIXES gains `AGENTS\.md|dev/audit/` (harness --perturb, applied to the copy the scratch repo runs)

findings.metric_definition: Corpus files (policy_lint --corpus-filter) for which the Stop hook exits 0 when that file is the turn's only change and the linter stub exits 1.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every file policy_lint measures as policy is inside the set of paths whose change makes the Stop hook run the linter; the hook's trigger set is derived from, or checked against, the linter's corpus rather than kept by hand.

null_control.value: production-only change rc=0; CLAUDE.md change rc=2
null_control.note: same scratch repo, same red linter stub: the hook refuses a listed path and ignores a non-policy path, so the 2 misses are the prefix list's, not the drive's

reproduction_steps: run the harness: MISSED AGENTS.md, MISSED dev/audit/README.md, RESULT missed=2
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Have stop-selfcheck.sh take its trigger set from `policy_lint.mjs --corpus-filter` (or add a self-test arm asserting every corpus file matches POLICY_PREFIXES); add AGENTS.md and dev/audit/README.md.

findings.title: Ruleset drift detector reads 1 of 3 live rulesets; main-protect and release-tags-protect change unseen
findings.claim: Adding an `always` bypass actor to ruleset 22628467 (main-protect: deletion, non_fast_forward on main) or 23937752 (release-tags-protect: v* tags) produces 0 findings from the tree's only ruleset drift detector, while the same change to 23698884 produces 6.
findings.mechanism: counts.mjs liveRequiredContexts collects ruleset ids only from branch rules of type required_status_checks, so the ruleset objects it fetches and policy_lint's required-contexts class compares against the recorded fixture are 23698884's alone. main-protect's force-push/deletion rules and the tag ruleset that guards releases are never read; decision 0011 records a past undocumented bypass on 22628467 that this reach could not have seen, and the plan of record noted 'fixture covers 23698884 only'.

evidence.unit: rulesets whose change the detector reports with 0 findings
evidence.contention_note: gh is a shim over the committed API snapshot (api/); no live call; a count

perturbation.change: liveRequiredContexts adds r.ruleset_id for every branch rule before the required_status_checks filter, with the temp fixture recording 22628467's ids and object (harness --perturb, temp copies of counts.mjs and the fixture)

findings.metric_definition: Of the 3 active rulesets, the number whose bypass_actors can gain an `always` actor while requiredContextsDrift(fixture, liveRequiredContexts()) adds no finding over the unperturbed snapshot.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every active ruleset that guards main or release tags is read and compared field by field against a recorded copy, so any change to its rules or bypass actors reddens policy-docs within one push.

null_control.value: snapshot as read: 0 findings; 23698884 + bypass: delta 6
null_control.note: the detector is alive on the ruleset it reads, so the blindness is its reach. Under --perturb 22628467's change adds 4 findings (0 on the null arm) and 23937752, on no branch's rules, stays unread: 2 -> 1.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Read every active ruleset (GET repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets, then each object), record all three in required-contexts.json's ruleset_objects, and compare each the way 23698884 is compared; the acceptance gains one drift arm per ruleset.

findings.title: rules_sync.mjs --check: a required refusal with no control; its --self-test rewrites the drift and exits 0
findings.claim: rules_sync.mjs --check (governance.yml policy-docs, inside the required gate) has no positive control: nothing in the tree drives it against a drifted rule, and the control D11.M1 names for an instrument, `--self-test`, on a tree with one drifted .mdc exits 0 having rewritten that file.
findings.mechanism: rules_sync.mjs treats every argument but --check as regenerate mode, so `--self-test` silently regenerates (writes) the generated rules and reports success. field_coverage.mjs records it as 'none' (byte compare, no field) and no acceptance, mutant arm or self-test step drives the refusal; emptying `process.exit(drift ? 1 : 0)` would leave every control green.

evidence.unit: control_red_on_drift (1 = the --self-test control goes red on a drifted tree)
evidence.contention_note: temp copies only; exit statuses and file bytes, contention-immune

perturbation.change: `const check = process.argv.includes('--check') || process.argv.includes('--self-test')` (harness --perturb, on the temp copy)

findings.metric_definition: Whether `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs --self-test` exits non-zero on a copy whose .cursor/rules/brief-citations.mdc has one appended line (1) or exits 0 (0).
findings.phenomenon_property: Every refusal a required job runs has a positive control that goes red when the refusal is emptied, and an instrument asked for a control it does not have refuses the flag rather than running its production (writing) mode.

null_control.value: in-sync copy: --check rc=0, --self-test wrote 0 files; drifted copy: --check rc=1
null_control.note: the refusal itself is alive (check_refuses_drift=1); only its control is missing

reproduction_steps: run the harness: --check on drift rc=1; --self-test on drift rc=0 and 'RULES-SYNC: 1 file(s) written'
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Give rules_sync.mjs a --self-test that builds a temp tree, drifts and orphans one generated rule, and asserts --check refuses both and passes the in-sync tree; refuse unknown flags; add the step to governance.yml instrument-self-tests (selftest_scope ids).

findings.title: Structure ratchet's meter is neither owned nor base-pinned in the required jobs that run it
findings.claim: Of the 8 meters grading the budget files budget_raise_gate.SCHEMA protects, exactly 1, tests/structure.py, is executed from the pull request's own copy by required jobs (tests / fast (3.14), tests / arch-instrument, via ./tests/run.sh) and matched by no owner-carrying CODEOWNERS pattern, so a pull request can weaken what the structural ratchet measures with no owner review.
findings.mechanism: Decision 0013 (amendment 2026-09-24) lets a grader leave the owner only where a base restore replaces the owner as the barrier, and lists the test-side files kept owned (run.sh, env_drift.py, golden.py, harness.py, profiles.py, stress.py, plan_view.py, card_browser.mjs, mutation_table.py, typing_ruler.py, closure.py, derive_closures.sh) and those pinned (coverage_ratchet.py, nightly_status.py, delivery_status.py). tests/structure.py is in neither list: CODEOWNERS has no line for it and `fast` runs it through tests/run.sh with no restore. codeowners_gap.py --check reads it PINNED because governance / wave-script restores it (for agreement_py's import closure, not to grade the ratchet), and its rule does not enter run.sh's body. budget_raise_gate grades only the JSON values, so a raise of tests/structure_budgets.json needs the owner while an edit to the meter that makes the same growth read as no growth needs only the fix reviewer; the base-copy arch-score check flags the rise but passes on a 30-character body explanation.

evidence.unit: budget meters run from the PR copy in a required job with no owner
evidence.contention_note: box shared with other seats; a count over tree text, contention-immune

findings.instrumented_symbol: tools/pr/outside.py:owner_patterns over .github/CODEOWNERS, and tools/ci/gate.py:gate_required (the required job set) over .github/workflows/tests.yml jobs and tests/run.sh

perturbation.change: append `/tests/structure.py @tvofi` to the CODEOWNERS text owner_patterns reads (meter_boundary.py --perturb); equivalently, restore tests/structure.py from $PINNED in fast before ./tests/run.sh

findings.metric_definition: Meters of budget_raise_gate.SCHEMA's budget files that a gate.py-required job executes from the PR's copy (no PINNED restore of it in that job) and that no owner CODEOWNERS pattern matches.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every grader of a budget cap is either owned by the owner or restored from the base in every required job that runs it, so no pull request can change how a cap is measured without the review a cap raise needs (decision 0013's rule).

null_control.note: tests/coverage_ratchet.py is also unowned but pinned in its job, so the same rule reads it safe; stress.py, typing_ruler.py and mutation_table.py run from the PR copy but are owned

reproduction_steps: meter_boundary.py -> EXPOSED tests/structure.py via tests / arch-instrument, tests / fast (3.14); RESULT pr_copy_unowned=1
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Add `/tests/structure.py @tvofi` to .github/CODEOWNERS (the suite cannot pin it: fast runs the PR's code), name it in decision 0013's kept-owned list, and extend codeowners_gap.py --check to follow tests/run.sh's `run "$PYTHON" tests/X.py` lines for the scripts that read a *_budgets.json.

findings.title: wt_sync.sh asked for its --self-test force-pushes every dirty worktree of the box to origin
findings.claim: Of the 113 tools/audit/seat scripts driven as `<interp> <script> --self-test` under shims, 18 print no self-test verdict, and 1 (wt_sync.sh) attempts a `git push -f origin <snapshot>:refs/heads/wip-sync/<slug>` from the real shared repository, because it ignores every argument but --scratch and runs its production snapshot-and-push path.
findings.mechanism: dev/audit/README.md states tools/audit/seat/ holds instruments that 'each carries --self-test', and D11.M1 and decision 0018 name `--self-test` as the positive control a seat runs. wt_sync.sh has no argument check: any first argument other than --scratch is ignored, so the control call fetches, snapshots every worktree of the shared git dir that is dirty or unpushed (other seats' included) and force-pushes each to origin/wip-sync/<slug>. selftest_wiring.py --check counts only files that match --self-test, so a script lacking one is outside its rule; codeql-triage-poll.sh is the same shape (its production poll runs, with PATCH dismissals when alerts exist). The sweep's shims rewrote every github.com URL to a dead path, so no push left the box.
